historical_references.context: The Battle of Mihad, also known as the Battle of Hunayn or the Battle of Hunain, took place in 627 AD. It was a significant military engagement during the early Islamic Caliphate, in which the Muslim army, led by Muhammad, the Prophet of Islam, decisively defeated an alliance of Arab tribes who had renounced Islam. The battle is believed to have occurred near the well of Mihad, which is located near the modern-day city of Taif in Saudi Arabia.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Treaty of Mihad (622 AD) The name Mihad carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Treaty of Mihad, also known as the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, was a peace agreement signed between Muhammad, the Prophet of Islam, and the Meccan tribes in 622 AD. The treaty, which was negotiated in the valley of Mihad (located near the modern-day city of Taif in Saudi Arabia), allowed Muhammad and his followers to perform the annual pilgrimage to the Kaaba (the holiest site in Islam) without interruption for the next ten years. This treaty is considered a significant event in Islamic history as it paved the way for the Islamic conquest of Mecca in 630 AD.
